name: Fribourg
summary: Fribourg was founded by the Zähringen in 1157, came under Kyburg, Habsburg and Savoy, then grew by buying and conquering Savoyard and Gruyère land until 1555, shared Murten, Schwarzenburg, Orbe-Echallens and Grandson with Bern until 1798, and got Murten alone in 1803.

stops.title: Zähringen found the town
text: In 1157 Duke Berchtold IV of Zähringen founds the town of Fribourg in a bend of the Saane river. The Zähringen are the strongest lords in this part of the Empire.

The land around belongs to many lords. The Bishop of Lausanne holds Bulle, Riaz and La Roche. The counts of Gruyère rule the upper Saane valley. Small noble families hold most villages. Murten and Kerzers are old estates of the Burgundian kings.

stops.title: Habsburg buys Fribourg
text: In 1218 the Zähringen family dies out. The counts of Kyburg inherit Fribourg. When they die out in 1263, the town puts itself under Count Rudolf of Habsburg.
In 1277 Rudolf, now king, makes the Kyburg heirs sell the town to his sons. Fribourg stays under Habsburg until 1452.
In the west, Peter II of Savoy takes Romont, Moudon and Payerne in the years after 1240. About 1255 Murten also comes under Savoy.

stops.title: Fribourg joins the Confederation
text: In 1481 Fribourg becomes a member of the Confederation. Its land is the city and the 'Old Countryside' (Alte Landschaft) around it. It also owns Montagny, bought in 1478, and Illens and Plaffeien, taken in the Burgundian Wars.

Fribourg rules some land together with Bern. These are common lordships (land ruled by two or more cantons, through a governor). Grasburg (Schwarzenburg) is shared since 1423. Murten, Grandson, Orbe and Echallens are shared since the Burgundian Wars of 1476.
Most of the south and west of today's canton still belongs to Savoy, to the Bishop of Lausanne or to the Count of Gruyère.

text: Fribourg buys more lordships, for example Pont in 1483 and Jaun from 1502.

Fribourg rules the new land as bailiwicks (land ruled by a governor sent from the city).

stops.title: Helvetic canton of Fribourg
text: In 1798 the French army ends the old order. Fribourg becomes a canton of the Helvetic Republic. The bailiwicks are gone, and all people have the same rights.

Fribourg also gets the districts of Payerne and Avenches until 1802.

name: Vaud
summary: Vaud was given to the Bishop of Lausanne in 1011 and taken over by Savoy in the 13th century; Bern conquered it step by step (Aigle 1475, most of Vaud 1536, Pays-d'Enhaut 1555), shared Orbe-Echallens and Grandson with Fribourg, and Vaud became a free canton in 1798–1803.

After 1032 the kingdom goes to the German emperors. Many noble families and monasteries also hold land in Vaud.

stops.title: Savoy takes over Vaud
text: In the 13th century the counts of Savoy come into Vaud. In 1219 the bishop gives Moudon to Savoy as a fief (land held from a higher lord).
From 1240 to 1260 Peter II of Savoy wins the loyalty of most lords of Vaud. He also gets Payerne. Savoy already holds the Chablais around Aigle.

The bishop keeps Lausanne, Lavaux, Lucens and Avenches. Other lords keep their own land, for example the lords of Grandson and, in the Pays-d'Enhaut, the counts of Gruyère. From the 14th century these lands count as fiefs of Savoy.

sources.supports: Bern takes Aigle and Bex

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: ebnete den Bernern und Freiburgern den Weg zur Annexion des Waadtländer Besitzes der de Chalon (Grandson, Orbe, Echallens)
sources.supports: Bern and Fribourg take Grandson, Orbe and Echallens

sources.title: HLS: Grandson (Herrschaft, Bezirk)
sources.quote: bis 1798 gemeine Herrschaft von Bern und Freiburg
sources.supports: They rule them together as common lordships until 1798

stops.title: Bernese Vaud
text: In 1536 Bern conquers Vaud from Savoy. It also takes Lausanne from the bishop and brings the Reformation. Fribourg takes the eastern part (today in the canton of Fribourg).
Bern divides Vaud into bailiwicks (land ruled by a governor sent from Bern). In 1555 Bern adds the Pays-d'Enhaut from the bankrupt Count of Gruyère.
Bern also holds Gex and land south of Lake Geneva, but gives it back to Savoy in 1564–1567. Vaud stays under Bern until 1798.

layers.name: Shared Bern and Fribourg
layers.label: Grandson, Orbe, Echallens: ruled by Bern and Fribourg together

layers.name: Aigle
layers.label: Aigle: ruled by Bern since 1475

layers.name: Pays-d'Enhaut
layers.label: Pays-d'Enhaut: Bernese bailiwick since 1555

layers.name: Pays de Vaud
layers.label: Pays de Vaud: Bernese bailiwicks since 1536 (not a canton yet)

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Im Frühling 1536 eroberten Berner Truppen, angeführt von Hans Franz Nägeli, unter Berufung auf den Vertrag von Saint-Julien (1530) die Waadt.
sources.supports: In 1536 Bern conquers Vaud from Savoy

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Nach der Flucht des Bischofs Sébastien de Montfalcon wurde dessen Besitz konfisziert.
sources.supports: Bern takes Lausanne from the bishop

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Das reformatorische Gedankengut verbreitete sich in der Waadt erst, als Bern nach der Lausanner Disputation vom Oktober 1536 den neuen Glauben einführte.
sources.supports: Bern brings the Reformation

sources.title: HLS: Freiburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Dieses gemeinsame Interesse führte 1536 zur militärischen Besetzung der Waadt durch die beiden Orte, die das eroberte Gebiet unter sich aufteilten
sources.supports: Fribourg takes the eastern part

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Die der Waadt am 13. Mai 1536 verliehenen Satzungen teilten das Land in Landvogteien ein
sources.supports: Bern divides Vaud into bailiwicks

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: nach dem Bankrott des Grafen von Greyerz 1555 mit dem Pays d'Enhaut noch eine weitere dazukam
sources.supports: In 1555 Bern adds the Pays-d'Enhaut

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Im Vertrag von Lausanne 1564 musste Bern die Landvogteien Gex, Ternier-Gaillard und Thonon dem Herzog von Savoyen zurückgeben
sources.supports: Bern gives Gex and land south of Lake Geneva back to Savoy (1564)

sources.title: HLS: Genf (Kanton)
sources.quote: gab Bern dem Herzog das Pays de Gex und die Dörfer des Genevois zurück, ein Vorgang, der 1567 in die Tat umgesetzt wurde
sources.supports: The return is carried out by 1567

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: erst die Waadtländer Revolution 1798 beendete die Fremdherrschaft
sources.supports: Vaud stays under Bern until 1798

stops.title: Lemanic Republic and canton Léman
text: In January 1798 Vaud breaks free from Bern and declares the Lemanic Republic. Soon after, it becomes the canton of Léman in the Helvetic Republic.
The common lordships and Aigle join the new canton. But the districts of Payerne and Avenches go to the canton of Fribourg until 1802.

layers.name: Payerne and Avenches
layers.label: Payerne and Avenches: part of canton Fribourg 1798–1802

layers.name: Canton of Léman
layers.label: Canton of Léman (Helvetic Republic)

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: rief eine Handvoll Patrioten in Lausanne und Vevey in der Nacht vom 24. Januar 1798 die Lemanische Republik aus
sources.supports: In January 1798 the Lemanic Republic is declared

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Während der Helvetischen Republik hiess die Waadt Kanton Léman
sources.supports: Vaud becomes the canton of Léman in the Helvetic Republic

sources.title: HLS: Echallens (Vogtei, Bezirk)
sources.quote: dann gemeine Vogtei Berns und Freiburgs, seit 1798 Bezirk des Kantons Waadt
sources.supports: The common lordships join the new canton (Echallens)

sources.title: HLS: Grandson (Herrschaft, Bezirk)
sources.quote: bis 1798 gemeine Herrschaft von Bern und Freiburg, seit 1798 Bezirk des Kantons Waadt
sources.supports: The common lordships join the new canton (Grandson)

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Der neue Kanton Léman umfasste die von Bern abgetrennte Waadt mit Ausnahme der Distrikte Avenches und Payerne, die zum Kanton Freiburg kamen.
sources.supports: Aigle (Bernese Vaud) joins; Payerne and Avenches go to Fribourg

sources.title: HLS: Léman (Kanton)
sources.quote: mit Ausnahme der Distrikte Avenches und Payerne, die bis am 16.10.1802 Freiburg angegliedert waren
sources.supports: Payerne and Avenches are part of Fribourg until 1802

stops.title: Canton of Vaud
text: In 1802 Payerne and Avenches come back. With the Act of Mediation of 1803, Vaud becomes a full canton of the Confederation.
Since then, the borders have almost not changed. Only in 1862 a treaty with France changes the border in the Vallée des Dappes, a small valley in the Jura.

layers.name: Canton of Vaud
layers.label: Canton of Vaud: member since 1803

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Avenches und Payerne waren zwischen 1798 und 1802 freiburgische Distrikte
sources.supports: In 1802 Payerne and Avenches come back

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: vom Erlass der Mediationsakte (1803) an Kanton Waadt
sources.supports: With the Act of Mediation of 1803 Vaud becomes a canton

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Kanton der Eidgenossenschaft seit 1803.
sources.supports: A full canton of the Confederation since 1803

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: Seine Grenzen sind seit dem 16. Jahrhundert unverändert, ausser im Broyetal
sources.supports: Since then the borders have almost not changed

sources.title: HLS: Waadt
sources.quote: im Dappental, wo 1862 der Grenzverlauf mit Frankreich bereinigt wurde
sources.supports: In 1862 the border with France changes in the Vallée des Dappes

notes: Before 1798 Vaud was not a canton; its main body is drawn as 'core' only so the map has a base, and the label says who ruled it. Grandson, Orbe and Echallens drawn as the towns only (the lordships were larger). Lausanne in 1476 drawn as the city only (the bishop also held Lavaux and other land). Payerne and Avenches districts 1798–1802 drawn as Payerne, Avenches, Faoug and Corcelles-près-Payerne. The 1862 Dappes change is too small to draw. Early stops: Lavaux drawn as Lutry, Bourg-en-Lavaux, Chexbres, Puidoux, Rivaz and Saint-Saphorin; lords of Grandson drawn as the town only. The 1011 stop simplifies: the bishop had count's rights, but much land was held by other lords and monasteries.

name: Valais
summary: Valais was given to the Bishop of Sion in 999 and divided with Savoy in 1392; the seven Zenden of Upper Valais then conquered Lower Valais in 1475 and 1536 and ruled it until 1798, and after Helvetic, independent and French years Valais joined the Confederation as a canton in 1815.

stops.title: Bishop of Sion becomes count
text: In 999 King Rudolf III of Burgundy gives the county of Valais to the Bishop of Sion. So the bishop is also the lord of the land. From 1032 he is directly under the emperor.
In the west, the old Abbey of Saint-Maurice holds much land. From the 12th century the counts of Savoy are its protectors and rule the Chablais.

layers.name: Abbey of Saint-Maurice
layers.label: Abbey of Saint-Maurice and the Chablais (later Savoy)

layers.name: Bishop of Sion
layers.label: Prince-Bishop of Sion: county of Valais from 999

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Zwar erhielt der Bischof von Sitten von Rudolph III. 999 die Grafschaftsrechte über das Wallis
sources.supports: In 999 Rudolf III gives the county of Valais to the Bishop of Sion

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Er begründete damit das Fürstbistum Sitten, das 1032 reichsunmittelbar wurde.
sources.supports: From 1032 the bishop is directly under the emperor

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: der König gab der Abtei 1018 alle ihre Güter im Wallis zurück
sources.supports: The Abbey of Saint-Maurice holds much land

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: die im Chablais etablierten Grafen von Savoyen, Kastvögte der Abtei Saint-Maurice, ab dem 12. Jahrhundert das Gebiet zwischen Rhoneknie und Genfersee dominierten
sources.supports: From the 12th century the counts of Savoy are its protectors and rule the Chablais

stops.title: Bishop and Savoy divide Valais
text: In the 13th century Savoy pushes up the valley towards Sion. The village communities grow strong and become the Zenden (dizains).
In 1384 Savoy takes Martigny and Ardon-Chamoson. The peace of 1392 divides Valais: above the Morge stream near Conthey is the bishop and the Zenden, below it is Savoy.
In 1403 the bishop and the Zenden make a permanent alliance with Lucerne, Uri and Unterwalden.

layers.name: Savoy
layers.label: Lower Valais: Savoy (border at the Morge of Conthey)

layers.name: Bishop of Sion and Zenden
layers.label: Upper Valais: Bishop of Sion and the Zenden

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Im 13. Jahrhundert stiessen die Grafen von Savoyen ins mittlere Wallis vor
sources.supports: In the 13th century Savoy pushes up the valley towards Sion

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: sieben Gemeinden oder Zenden (lateinisch decima; desenus)
sources.supports: The village communities become the Zenden

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Martigny und Ardon-Chamoson (ab 1384 Savoyen)
sources.supports: In 1384 Savoy takes Martigny and Ardon-Chamoson

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Der Friedensvertrag von 1392 legte die Morge von Conthey als Grenze fest und beseitigte die jeweiligen Enklaven.
sources.supports: The peace of 1392 divides Valais at the Morge of Conthey

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: 1403 schlossen Bischof und Zenden ein ewiges Burg- und Landrecht mit Luzern, Uri und Unterwalden
sources.supports: In 1403 the bishop and the Zenden make a permanent alliance with Lucerne, Uri and Unterwalden

stops.title: Upper Valais allies with Swiss
text: Upper Valais is a land of seven communities, the Zenden (dizains), under the Bishop of Sion. In 1416–1417 they make an alliance with Lucerne, Uri and Unterwalden. So Valais becomes an ally (zugewandter Ort) of the Confederation, not a full member.
Lower Valais, west of the Morge stream near Sion, belongs to the Duke of Savoy.

layers.name: Seven Zenden
layers.label: Upper Valais: the seven Zenden and the Bishop of Sion

layers.name: Savoyard Lower Valais

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Spätestens mit der Erneuerung des Bündnisses 1416 und 1417 galt das Wallis als zugewandter Ort der Eidgenossenschaft.
sources.supports: In 1416–1417 the alliance is renewed; Valais becomes an ally (zugewandter Ort), not a member

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: sieben Gemeinden oder Zenden (lateinisch decima; desenus)
sources.supports: Upper Valais is a land of seven Zenden

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Der Friedensvertrag von 1392 legte die Morge von Conthey als Grenze fest
sources.supports: Lower Valais, west of the Morge, belongs to Savoy

stops.title: Conquest of Lower Valais
text: In the Burgundian Wars, the Upper Valaisans beat the Savoyard army at the Planta near Sion in 1475. They take Lower Valais down to Saint-Maurice.
The Zenden rule this land as a subject land (land with no vote, ruled by governors). Also in 1475 Valais makes an alliance with Bern.

layers.name: Monthey
layers.label: Monthey area: still Savoy

layers.name: Lower Valais
layers.label: Lower Valais to Saint-Maurice: ruled by the Zenden since 1475

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: im November 1475 Conthey und besiegte mit eidgenössischen Hilfstruppen das savoyische Heer auf der Planta in Sitten.
sources.supports: In 1475 the Upper Valaisans beat Savoy at the Planta near Sion

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: 1475 kam mit der Landvogtei Saint-Maurice (bis 1536 Landvogtei nid der Mors) ein weiteres hinzu
sources.supports: They take Lower Valais down to Saint-Maurice and rule it as subject land

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: als es 1475 in der Waadt einfiel und sich mit Bischof und Zenden gegen Savoyen verbündete
sources.supports: In 1475 Valais makes an alliance with Bern

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: im Zug der Eroberung der Waadt und des Chablais durch Bern 1536 Monthey und Evian
sources.supports: The Monthey area is still Savoyard until 1536 (map layer)

stops.title: Monthey kept, Chablais returned
text: In 1536 the Upper Valaisans take the rest of the Savoyard Chablais, south of Lake Geneva, as far as Evian.

In the Treaty of Thonon of 1569 Valais gives Evian and the Aulps valley back to Savoy. It keeps Monthey. The border is now at the Morge stream at Saint-Gingolph. Since then, the outer border of Valais has hardly changed.

layers.name: Lower Valais
layers.label: Lower Valais with Monthey: ruled by the Zenden

layers.name: Seven Zenden
layers.label: Upper Valais: the seven Zenden

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: im Zug der Eroberung der Waadt und des Chablais durch Bern 1536 Monthey und Evian
sources.supports: In 1536 the Upper Valaisans take the Chablais as far as Evian

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Seit dem Vertrag von Thonon 1569, in dem die Morge von Saint-Gingolph als Grenze zwischen dem Fürstbistum und dem Herzogtum Savoyen festgelegt wurde
sources.supports: Treaty of Thonon 1569; the border is at the Morge at Saint-Gingolph

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: gingen Evian und das Vallée d'Aulps an Savoyen zurück und die Morge bei Saint-Gingolph wurde als Westgrenze festgelegt
sources.supports: In 1569 Valais gives Evian and the Aulps valley back; border at the Morge at Saint-Gingolph

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: blieben die politischen Grenzen des Wallis, abgesehen von kleineren Bereinigungen, unverändert
sources.supports: Since then the outer border has hardly changed

sources.title: HLS: Saint-Maurice (Kastlanei, Bezirk)
sources.quote: Die Herrschaft der Zenden über die Landvogtei S., die neben S. acht weitere Kastlaneien umfasste, wurde mit dem Vertrag von Thonon 1569 bestätigt.
sources.supports: Lower Valais (with Monthey) stays under the Zenden

stops.title: Lower Valais free, Helvetic canton
text: In early 1798 Lower Valais declares itself free, and Upper Valais accepts this. Then Valais becomes a canton of the Helvetic Republic. All its people now have the same rights.

layers.name: Canton of Valais
layers.label: Canton of Valais (Helvetic Republic)

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Nachdem sich Monthey und weitere Gemeinden der Bewegung angeschlossen hatten, gestand der Landrat dem Unterwallis am 22. Februar Freiheit und Unabhängigkeit zu.
sources.supports: In early 1798 Lower Valais declares itself free and Upper Valais accepts this

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: 1798-1802 Kanton der Helvetischen Republik
sources.supports: Valais becomes a canton of the Helvetic Republic

uncertain: All people of Valais now have the same rights.

stops.title: French département of Simplon
text: In 1802 Valais becomes a separate state, the independent Republic of Valais. Napoleon builds a military road over the Simplon Pass (1805).
In 1810 France annexes Valais. It becomes the French département (province) of Simplon until 1813.

layers.name: Département du Simplon
layers.label: Valais: French département of Simplon 1810–1813

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: Es bildete vom 30. August 1802 bis 1810 eine unabhängige Republik
sources.supports: From 1802 to 1810 Valais is an independent republic (corrects 'Rhodanic Republic')

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: 1805 napoleonische Militärstrasse über den Simplon
sources.supports: Napoleon's military road over the Simplon (1805)

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: 1810-1813 Departement Simplon im französischen Kaiserreich
sources.supports: In 1810 France annexes Valais as the département of Simplon until 1813

stops.title: Valais joins as a canton
text: In 1815 Valais joins the Confederation as a full canton. Neuchâtel and Geneva also join in 1814–1815.
Since then, the borders have hardly changed.

layers.name: Canton of Valais
layers.label: Canton of Valais: member since 1815

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: ab 1815 Republik und Kanton der Schweizerischen Eidgenossenschaft
sources.supports: In 1815 Valais joins the Confederation as a canton

sources.title: HLS: Genf (Kanton)
sources.quote: Kanton der Eidgenossenschaft seit 1815.
sources.supports: Geneva also joins in 1815

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: hatten am 12. September 1814 von der Tagsatzung die Aufnahme Neuenburgs als 21. Kanton erreicht
sources.supports: Neuchâtel is accepted as a canton in 1814

sources.title: HLS: Wallis
sources.quote: blieben die politischen Grenzen des Wallis, abgesehen von kleineren Bereinigungen, unverändert
sources.supports: Since then the borders have hardly changed

notes: The seven Zenden drawn as today's districts Goms, Brig, Visp, Raron, Leuk, Sierre, Sion and Hérens (Hérens counted with the Sion Zenden). Savoyard Lower Valais before 1475 drawn as districts Conthey, Martigny, Entremont, Saint-Maurice and Monthey; the real border at the Morge near Sion and the status of Martigny (episcopal but Savoyard-held) are simplified. The Chablais land 1536–1569 (Evian, Aulps) is outside Switzerland and is in the text only. The 999 stop simplifies: Savoy's rule in the Chablais grew only from the 12th century. In 1392 Martigny is drawn whole with Savoy.

name: Neuchâtel
summary: Neuchâtel was a castle of the Burgundian kings, then a county of its own noble family allied with the Swiss; it united with Valangin in 1592, came under the King of Prussia in 1707, joined the Confederation as a canton in 1814/1815 and became a republic in 1848.

stops.title: Castle in the Kingdom of Burgundy
text: In 1011 Neuchâtel ('new castle') is named for the first time. King Rudolf III of Burgundy gives it, with other royal estates, to his bride Irmingard.
After 1032 the land belongs to the Empire.

layers.name: Kingdom of Burgundy
layers.label: Kingdom of Burgundy, from 1032 the Empire

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Letzteres wurde offensichtlich kurz vor 1011, dem Jahr seiner Ersterwähnung, gebaut.
sources.supports: In 1011 Neuchâtel is named for the first time

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Die königlichen Güter, mit denen 1011 Irmingard, die Verlobte des Burgunderkönigs Rudolf III. ausgestattet wurde, umfassten Neuenburg (novum castellum)
sources.supports: Rudolf III gives it, with other royal estates, to his bride Irmingard

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Ab 1033 gelangte das neuenburgische Gebiet nach und nach mit dem Königreich Burgund ans Reich.
sources.supports: After 1032 the land belongs to the Empire

stops.title: Lords of Neuchâtel and Valangin
text: A noble family takes the name of Neuchâtel and rules the land. In 1214 the town of Neuchâtel gets a charter of freedoms. About 1218 the family divides its land.

Valangin, with the Val-de-Ruz and later the mountains, goes to a related branch (Aarberg). It is first named in 1242. In 1288 the counts lose their direct link to the emperor and come under the Chalon family.

layers.label: Le Cerneux-Péquignot: County of Burgundy (Franche-Comté)

layers.name: County of Neuchâtel
layers.label: Lords (later counts) of Neuchâtel

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Die schon 1185 erwähnten Bürger von Neuenburg erhielten 1214 einen dem Gewohnheitsrecht von Besançon folgenden Freiheitsbrief.
sources.supports: In 1214 the town gets a charter of freedoms

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Als die gemeinsame Herrschaft um 1218 zu Ende ging, teilten Ulrich III. und sein Neffe Berchtold das Territorium unter sich auf
sources.supports: About 1218 the family divides its land

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Nach der Teilung zogen die von Aarberg, ein Zweig der Neuenburg-Nidau, die 1242 erstmals erwähnte Herrschaft Valangin an sich.
sources.supports: Valangin goes to the Aarberg branch; first named in 1242

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: 1288 wurde die Reichsunmittelbarkeit der geschwächten und zu einfachen Herren herabgesunkenen von Neuenburg aufgehoben
sources.supports: In 1288 they lose their direct link to the emperor

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Rudolf I. von Habsburg unterstellte sie der Oberlehensherrschaft der von Chalon
sources.supports: They come under the Chalon family

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: 1814 die im Pariser Frieden beschlossene Angliederung des Dorfs Le Cerneux-Péquignot
sources.supports: Le Cerneux-Péquignot is outside Neuchâtel until 1814 (map layer)

stops.title: County allied with Bern
text: Neuchâtel is a county. From 1395 it belongs to the counts of Freiburg (in Breisgau). The count has alliances of citizenship (Burgrecht) with Swiss cities: with Bern since 1308 (renewed in 1406), with Fribourg since 1290 and with Solothurn since 1369. So it is an ally of the Swiss, not a member.
The mountains and the Val-de-Ruz form a separate lordship, Valangin.

layers.label: Lordship of Valangin (Aarberg-Valangin family)

layers.name: County of Neuchâtel
layers.label: County of Neuchâtel: counts of Freiburg from 1395 (ally of the Swiss)

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Als das lokale Geschlecht der Herren von Neuenburg 1395 erlosch, ging die Grafschaft an die aus Süddeutschland stammenden Familien von Freiburg und von Hochberg über.
sources.supports: From 1395 the county belongs to the counts of Freiburg

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: insbesondere mit Freiburg (1290), Bern (1308), Solothurn (1369) und Luzern (1501)
sources.supports: Burgrecht alliances with Fribourg (1290), Bern (1308) and Solothurn (1369)

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Der Graf von Neuenburg und sein Sohn leisten vor dem Schultheiss und dem Rat von Bern den Eid anlässlich des Burgrechtsvertrags von 1406.
sources.supports: The alliance with Bern is renewed in 1406

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Obgleich Neuenburg ein zugewandter Ort der Eidgenossenschaft war, besass es keinen Sitz in der Tagsatzung.
sources.supports: It is an ally of the Swiss, not a member

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Die Herren von Valangin, die sich mit ihrer Lehensabhängigkeit schwertaten, behielten allerdings bis zum Ende des 16. Jahrhunderts eine eigenständige Verwaltung.
sources.supports: Valangin is a separate lordship

stops.title: Valangin joins the county
text: From 1458 the Hochberg family rules, and from 1504 the Orléans-Longueville family. From 1512 to 1529 the Swiss cantons occupy Neuchâtel and rule it together through governors. Then they give it back.
In 1592 the lordship of Valangin is united with the county. Now the state has almost its present size.

sources.supports: From 1458 the Hochberg family rules

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Die d'Orléans-Longueville (1504-1707)
sources.supports: From 1504 the Orléans-Longueville family

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: die Grafschaft während der Mailänderkriege vorsorglich zu besetzen und sie 1512-1529 durch Vögte verwalten zu lassen
sources.supports: From 1512 to 1529 the Swiss occupy Neuchâtel and rule it through governors

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: Nach einem langen Prozess vereinigte sich 1592 die Herrschaft Valangin mit der Grafschaft.
sources.supports: In 1592 Valangin is united with the county

sources.title: HLS: Neuenburg (Kanton)
sources.quote: an der Spitze eines Staats, dessen Grenzen fast mit jenen des heutigen Kantons übereinstimmten

stops.title: Canton and principality
text: In 1707 the King of Prussia becomes Prince of Neuchâtel. From 1806 to 1814 Napoleon gives the principality to his marshal Berthier.
In 1814 Neuchâtel gets Le Cerneux-Péquignot from France. On 12 September 1814 the Swiss Diet accepts Neuchâtel as the 21st canton. In 1815 it also gets all of Lignières.
Neuchâtel is now a Swiss canton and, at the same time, a principality of the King of Prussia.

name: Geneva
summary: Geneva was a bishop's city in the Empire surrounded by the counts of Geneva and later Savoy; it became an independent city-republic with scattered rural lands in 1536, was French from 1798 to 1813, and in 1815–1816 got communes from France and Savoy that link it to Switzerland.

stops.title: Bishop's city in the Empire
text: Geneva belongs to the Kingdom of Burgundy. In 1032 the last king dies, and his land goes to the German emperor.
The bishop rules the city. From the 11th century the counts of Geneva are the strongest lords in the land around it.

stops.title: Savoy buys the county
text: The bishop holds the city and rural districts (mandements) such as Peney and Jussy. The priory of Saint-Victor and the cathedral chapter hold other villages. The lords of Gex rule the land to the north-west.
The counts of Geneva die out in 1394. In 1402 Amadeus VIII of Savoy buys their county. By 1424 he also buys the rights of all other heirs. Now Savoy surrounds Geneva and tries to control the city.

stops.title: Independent city-republic
text: In 1526 Geneva makes an alliance (Burgrecht) with Bern and Fribourg. In 1536 the bishop leaves, the city takes the Reformation and becomes an independent republic, an ally of the Swiss.

Geneva takes the bishop's rural lands: the mandements (districts) of Peney and Jussy, and Céligny. It also has rights in villages of the Saint-Victor priory and the cathedral chapter, but Savoy claims many of them.
The lands around them belong to Savoy or, from 1601, to France (Pays de Gex). Many Genevan villages are enclaves.

text: Geneva is free again at the end of 1813. In 1815 it joins the Confederation as a canton.

By the Second Treaty of Paris of 20 November 1815, France gives Geneva all or part of Versoix, Collex-Bossy, Le Grand-Saconnex, Pregny, Vernier and Meyrin. Now Geneva touches Vaud and Switzerland by land.
